notes:
Zero turns start in this stretch. There is no bold run anywhere in the fragment: it is fifteen consecutive

paragraphs of one continuous speech that began before the fragment and continues past it. Context check in data/raw/senado/taquigraficas/2003-05-07_r07_ESPECIAL.html: the label preceding this material is 'Sra. Negre de Alonso. --' and the next label after it is the chair's, a long way downstream, with nothing in between - so the whole fragment sits inside that one senator's speech. I considered and rejected reading this as an inserted document. It is a dense, scholarly passage on the 1853 Constitution, article 19 and the case law, quoting Alberdi and citing Sampay, Sagüés, Caballero, Legarre, Nino, Belluscio and Bacqué - the kind of text that is often handed in for the record rather than spoken. But it is floor speech, for three reasons: it uses the first person of someone addressing the chamber ('a la que adherimos plenamente', 'otras voces que no puedo dejar de nombrar'); it is typeset in exactly the same

pattern as the ordinary speech on either side of it, with no change of font, no indent and no italic block of the sort this file uses to set off inserted material; and no stenographer's note introduces it. Nothing here is a separate speaker, so no speaker was invented. This file's markup differs from the other two stretches I annotated: lowercase tags, and every paragraph wrapped

... followed by a stray empty . That empty run closes each paragraph and carries no text; it is not furniture and not an event, and I did not record it. Anything that keys on font changes to find labels will see a font change at every single paragraph in this fragment and must not treat any of them as a turn. No events, no headings and no furniture (no back-links, no footnote pointers, no contents entries, no sign-off) appear. The quoted constitutional text in double quotation marks ('Las acciones privadas de los hombres...') is quoted aloud by the senator and is part of her turn, not an insertion.
